html:
Kashi was a small ancient kingdom around the city of Varanasi on the Ganges, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of the 6th century BCE.

Kashi was old and prestigious, famed for its cloth and its holy city. It fought long wars with its neighbour Kosala and lost. By the Buddha's lifetime Kosala ruled it, and a Kosalan king gave a village of Kashi as a dowry when his daughter married Bimbisara of Magadha.

Just outside Varanasi, at Sarnath, the Buddha gave his first sermon; see the Buddha teaches. Varanasi itself outlived every kingdom around it and is still one of the holiest cities of Hinduism.
sum: Kashi was a small ancient kingdom around the city of Varanasi on the Ganges, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of the 6th century BCE.
